transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm explaining this right, but... well, it’s a little embarrassing, honestly. I feel a bit silly even being here for it. 

I teach preschool, and... well, what brings me in is that I have this reaction to balloons. I know that sounds ridiculous for a teacher, right? But the second I spot them at school, even if they're all the way across the hallway, my chest just tightens up. I kind of just... freeze for a moment before I can even think clearly about what I’m supposed to be doing with my students. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job at work, and I'm hoping I can get a handle on this, if that makes sense?
When you see balloons, do you ever experience symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or feeling like you’re losing control, in addition to your chest tightening up?

No, no, I don't think I've ever felt like I was losing control or anything extreme like that. I mean, my heart might beat a little faster, maybe? But it's really just the chest tightness and that momentary freeze. I wouldn't say I'm sweating or panicking in a big way. It's more of just a strong discomfort, you know? I hope that's a normal way to describe it? I just try to keep it together for the kids, so I definitely don't let it get to a point where I'm losing control. Does that answer your question okay?
Do you find yourself avoiding places or situations where you might see balloons because of how they make you feel?

Um... well, I really try my best not to let it interfere, because I want to be a good teacher for the kids, you know? But... I guess, lately, I have been sort of... delegating a little bit. I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible at my job, but I've been asking my aides to handle the birthday circles. And if there's a school festival or something, I might just kind of subtly move away from the tables that have balloons tied to them. 

If I absolutely have to stay in the room, I just... I keep my distance and really focus on getting through it without looking directly at them. Is that an okay way to handle it for now? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.

Do you feel significant distress or find that this reaction to balloons is starting to interfere with your ability to do your job or enjoy your daily life, even if you're managing it by avoiding certain situations?

Um... well, I guess... I mean, I really don't want to make a big deal out of it, because I love my job so much, but... yeah, it is starting to get a little bit in the way. I hope that doesn't sound like I'm a bad teacher. 

It's just that, like I mentioned, I've had to hand off the normal classroom celebrations to my aides, which... you know, I should be doing. And then recently, there was this school festival, and I had actually planned this whole art table for the kids. I was really excited about it. But they tied balloons to the chairs, and I just... I couldn't do it. I had to step away and miss helping with it. My supervisor actually noticed, which was really embarrassing. I just want to be reliable, you know? Do you think it's bad that it's affecting my work like this? I'm really trying my best to fix it.
Is your discomfort limited to balloons, or do you also feel similar reactions to other things, like party decorations or similar objects?

Um... no, it's really just the balloons. I mean, streamers, confetti, party hats... all of that is totally fine. I actually love decorating for the kids' birthdays, I really do! It's just... specifically the balloons that give me that tight feeling. 

I don't have a problem with anything else, I promise. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so I can get back to being the best teacher I can be. Is it normal for it to just be one specific thing like that?
When you're around balloons, does the tightness in your chest start right away, or does it build up over time, and how long does it usually last?

Um... well, it's pretty much right away. I don't want to sound dramatic, but... yeah, the second I spot them, even if they're just, you know, way down at the other end of the hallway at school, it just hits me. 

My chest gets all tight, and I kind of... freeze for a second. Just for a moment, though! I promise I don't just stand there forever. It just takes me a second to sort of gather myself and remember what I'm supposed to be doing. And then the feeling usually stays until I can get away from them. I try really hard to hide it so the kids don't notice. Is that... does that sound like a normal reaction to have? I just hope I'm explaining it right.
When you see balloons, do you feel an intense fear or anxiety that they might suddenly pop or come toward you?

Um... yeah, I guess that's exactly it. I mean, I know logically that a balloon in the classroom is probably just a decoration, you know? It's just there for the kids. But... when I see one that looks really stretched tight, or if it's just bobbing around near the children, I get this... well, it feels like it could just burst right in my face at any second. 

And I get so scared. It's almost silly, because I know the situation isn't actually dangerous, but the fear just feels so much bigger than it should be. I really try not to let it show, because I know it's an overreaction. Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound completely unreasonable for feeling that way.
Do you notice that your reaction to balloons happens every single time you see them, even if you're expecting them or they're in a calm, controlled setting like a store or someone's house?

Um... gosh, I'm actually not entirely sure. I guess I haven't really noticed if it happens every single time? 

I mean, if I know they're going to be somewhere—like the party aisle at the grocery store—I usually just... well, I just sort of walk down a different aisle. I really try not to make a fuss or let it become an issue for anyone else, you know? So I haven't really tested it in a calm setting where I'm expecting them, mostly because I just try to avoid looking at them altogether so I don't cause a scene. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I'm sorry if that's not very helpful... I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me. Is it alright that I don't really know for sure?
